- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 15–30% for short-term (1–7d) horizons.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or shows sharp drops, model underestimates; increase forecast lows by 10–25% for medium-term (8–21d) horizons.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 3x recent mean), model often overcorrects downward; apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 20–40% for 1–3d after spike.
- For 30d forecasts, model frequently fails to capture mean reversion; if sentiment is neutral or mixed, apply a “mean reversion bias” — adjust forecast toward 1.5–2x recent 7d average.
- If sentiment shows consistent upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.33), model tends to overreact; cap forecast growth at 1.2x recent 7d average for 14d+ horizons.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often underestimates volatility; increase forecast standard deviation by 10–20% for 1–7d horizons to reflect sentiment uncertainty.
